thread.title: Graphite Demand to Put World’s 5th Largest Mine Bank into Production

author: Brandon Manns
title: Graphite Demand to Put World’s 5th Largest Mine Bank into Production
text:
Graphite Demand to Put World’s 5th Largest Mine Bank into Production share on: 
Graphite Energy Corp. (OTCQB: GRXXF, CSE: GRE) is sitting on the World’s 5 th largest graphite mine, complete with infrastructure and a mill. This company makes no bones about looking to supply Tesla, Inc. (NASDAQ: TSLA) with graphite for its battery plant near Reno, Nevada. In fact, GRXXF, GRE stands to see its value SKYROCKET in the near term. 
The Lac Aux Bouleaux Property is comprised of 14 mineral claims in one contiguous block totaling 738.12 hectares land on NTS 31J05, near the town of Mont-Laurier in southern Québec. Lac Aux Bouleaux “LAB” is a world class graphite property that borders the only producing graphite in North America. 
A sampling program GRXXF, GRE announced in early January generated graphite samples with purity as high as 22%. That’s HUGE NEWS! “The results further confirm our team’s initial thoughts of high grade flake graphite on the property,” GRXXF, GRE noted in the Release. 
World-Class Mine 
The open pit mine in operation since 1989 with an onsite plant ranked 5th in the world production of graphite. The mine is operated by TIMCAL Graphite & Carbon which is a subsidiary of IMERYS S.A., a French multinational company. The mine has an average grade of 7.5% Cg (graphite carbon) and has been producing 50 different graphite products for various graphite end users around the globe. 
THINK OF IT! GRXXF, GRE has a producing mine – right next door! Operating with an AVERAGE GRADE OF 7.5% Cg (graphite Carbon). GRAPHITE ENERGY’S AVERAGE GRADE IS 10%!!! (See the chart, below; Red border identifies Graphite Energy Corporation’s property, the black border identifies TIMCAL.) 
CAN YOU SMELL THE MONEY? 
Management knows the ropes. The Company is led by Afzaal Pirzada, M.Sc. (Geology), P.Geo. President & C.E.O of Graphite Energy Corp . 
Pirzada is NO SLOUCH when it comes to Graphite or Lithium. Pirzada has 30 years’ experience as a geologist with expertise in lithium and rare metals elements, graphite, PGE and uranium. 
World Demand for Graphite is Growing – BIG TIME. Demand grew from 600,000 ton in 2000 to roughly 1.1 million ton in 2011. AND LIKE THE ENERGIZER BUNNY, DEMAND FOR GRAPHITE KEEPS GOING AND GOING AND GOING!!! 
More Than Pencils 
Graphite is used in many applications, not just pencils and GRXXF, GRE is ALL OVER IT! Take a look at what’s in store for this fabulous company… 
MOVE OVER TESLA. Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG), Apple (NASDAQ: APPL) and Farday Future are ALL looking to build battery factories that could DOUBLE DEMAND by 2023 . In fact, demand is so important, Farday Future hosted the first Global Supplier Summit in February, 2018. Attending where 200 representatives from 100 suppliers. 
Farday is planning on giving Tesla a run for the money with its own line of electric automobiles. Farday’s founder, YT Jia, was quoted as saying, “FF 91 is a new species. It’s more than an electric car – it’s the third Internet living space,” said YT, “It would be impossible to deliver a ground-breaking vehicle like FF 91 without alignment with our top suppliers.” 
Electric Car Sales Buoy Demand for Graphite 
With demand FOR GRAPHITE AND LITHIUM RISING, SO WILL GRXXF, GRE . Speculation arose that graphite could be in short supply because a large EV battery requires about 25kg (55lb) of graphite for the Li-ion anode. 
Purified natural flake graphite has a higher crystalline structure and offers better electrical and thermal conductivity than synthetic material. Switching to natural graphite will lower production cost with same or better Li-ion performance. 
Unprocessed natural graphite is much cheaper, and besides cost, natural graphite is more environmentally friendly than synthetic graphite; it also forms the base for graphene, a scientist’s dream. At the end of 2016, natural graphite accounts for 60-65% of the market share; synthetic is around 30% and alternatives such as lithium titanate, silicon and tin is 5%. Graphite Energy Corp is smack-dab in the running to become a world-class supplier of high-grade graphite to the Li-ion battery market for electric car manufacturers, such as Tesla and Farday. 
Solar Application 
Li-ion batteries aren’t the only application for GRXXf, GRE’s graphite mine. Battery powered homes will be the future and will increase demand for graphite by over 1000 times . Solar power batteries will be in every home in the years to come. Graphite offers untapped potential in terms of the efficiency of photovoltaic cells and what happens at night and during inclement weather. 
With 12 lithium ion battery “mega factories” set to come on line by 2020 according to Benchmark Mineral Intelligence (and 7 of those in China), owning more of the supply chain makes a great deal of strategic sense . 
Tesla’s solar power roofs are coming into their own, according to Musk’s company. With a 30% tax credit still available to homeowners, TESLA’s solar powered roofs are gaining consumer attention, though costs are still a factor. But on the PLUS SIDE, you don’t have to replace them every 10 years. 
Scientists at MIT claim to have come up with a carbon- graphite solar steam generator. MIT is reporting that it has created a new, cheap material — using a microwave, no less — that converts sunlight into steam with an amazing 85% efficiency. 
The new material, developed by MIT mechanical engineer Hadi Ghasemi, consists of a thin double-layered disc. The bottom layer consists of spongy carbon foam that doubles up as a flotation device and a thermal insulator that prevents solar energy from dissipating into the fluid underneath. The top layer — the active layer — consists of flakes of graphite that were exfoliated using a microwave. The microwave causes the graphite to bubble up “just like popcorn” according to Gang Chen, another researcher involved with the work. 
Graphite is a mineral that is quietly fueling the future of clean technology, and its applications in the battery market just keep growing and growing. Graphite grabbed investors’ attention when Tesla CEO Elon Musk, determined to provide the world with clean battery power for cars and homes, identified Graphite and Nickel as key elements in the lithium-ion battery cell mass. Musk even said that lithium ion batteries “ should be called Nickel-Graphite .” Minerals like these are vital to the growth of clean tech. Mining companies like SunPower Corp. (NASDAQ: SPWR), Global X Lithium (NYSE: LIT), First Solar (NASDAQ: FSLR), Alcoa Corp . (NYSE: AA), and Graphite Energy Corp. (CSE: GRE) (OTCQB: GRXXF) know this and are strategically mining the minerals of the future. 
The North American hotbed of graphite production is actually in Québec, Canada, where junior mining companies Mason Graphite Inc. (CSE: LLG) and Graphite Energy Corp. are rapidly assembling operations. 
Graphene, a form of carbon that results from the reduction of graphite, is the world’s most conductive material, and it offers a range of opportunities for advanced display technologies, communications systems and desalination solutions. Graphene is also going to be an essential component in the solar panel market, as home builders adopt solar power technology. 
Graphene is also produced at Graphite Energy Corp.’s Lac Aux Bouleaux (LAB) property in Québec, which is located right next to Imerys, the only actively producing mine in North America. Technical data obtained during discovery confirmed that LAB is a natural flake graphite mine, and natural graphite is what clean technology companies like Tesla need to gear the globe towards a green future. 
Can You Say Triple-Bagger? 
GRXXF, GRE traded as-high-as $1.55, though an abrupt drop in price has made the graphite mining company’s stock A REAL BARGAIN FOR INVESTORS. 
Graphite Energy Corp. (CSE: GRE) (OTCQB: GRXXF) has the lead on other mining juniors because the company has already completed the discovery phase at their Lac Aux Bouleaux Graphite property in Southern Québec. Technical data has confirmed that the mine contains natural, large flake graphite, which is the type of mineral companies like Tesla will need to power car and home battery packs. Actual drilling begins this week , positioning Graphite Energy Corp . as the first domestic junior mining company to bring the mineral to the North American market. 
Mason Graphite secured a $45 million private placement deal in January to be used for development and construction expenses at its Lac Guéret graphite mine in Northeastern Québec. Strategic investments in graphite production are on the rise as investors realize the mineral is a key ingredient in the growth of solar power and clean tech. All this bodes well for Graphite Energy Corp.’s burgeoning operations in the hotbed of North American graphite production.
